name: C16577
summary: Codeine-6-glucuronide (C6G) is a major active metabolite of codeine and may be responsible for as much as 60% of the analgesic effects of codeine. C6G exhibits decreased immunosuppressive effects compared to codeine.

pharmacology.text: Codeine-6-glucuronide (C6G) is a major active metabolite of codeine and may be responsible for as much as 60% of the analgesic effects of codeine.

uses.en: It is not used as a medicine on its own. It forms in the body after codeine is taken and is studied in research on how codeine relieves pain.
uses.zh: 它本身並不作為藥物使用。它是服用可待因後在體內生成的，主要用於研究可待因如何止痛。
uses.zhHans: 它本身并不作为药物使用。它是服用可待因后在体内生成的，主要用于研究可待因如何止痛。

sideEffects.en: Little is known about it on its own. As an active part of codeine's effect, it is thought to add to typical opioid effects such as drowsiness, constipation, nausea and, at high levels, slowed breathing.
sideEffects.zh: 它單獨的作用所知甚少。由於它是可待因藥效的活性成分之一，一般認為它會加重典型的鴉片類作用，例如嗜睡、便秘、噁心，濃度高時可能抑制呼吸。
sideEffects.zhHans: 它单独的作用所知甚少。由于它是可待因药效的活性成分之一，一般认为它会加重典型的鸦片类作用，例如嗜睡、便秘、恶心，浓度高时可能抑制呼吸。

fact.en: The liver makes it by attaching glucuronic acid, a sugar acid, to codeine. This step usually switches a drug off so it can be passed in urine, but this product stays active at opioid receptors.
fact.zh: 肝臟會把葡萄糖醛酸（一種糖酸）接到可待因上而生成它。這個步驟通常會讓藥物失去活性、方便從尿液排出，但這個產物仍能作用於鴉片類受體。
fact.zhHans: 肝脏会把葡萄糖醛酸（一种糖酸）接到可待因上而生成它。这个步骤通常会让药物失去活性、方便从尿液排出，但这个产物仍能作用于鸦片类受体。
